key_insight: A DFT-informed all-atom model reproduces the skeletal density of resorcinol-formaldehyde aerogels and tracks iron incorporation.
engineering_relevance: The model provides a starting point for screening fillers and dopants for RF aerogels, with potential applications in thermoelectric functionalization and thermal insulation.
method: Optimize the RF base unit with DFT and compare its infrared spectrum with experiment.
Benchmark classical force fields against DFT for branched RF units, selecting COMPASS II.
Simulate a 15,012-atom RF system using NVT and NPT molecular dynamics, then add 5 wt% iron.
evidence_signal: The calculated infrared spectrum agreed with experiment, the simulated skeletal density was 1.296 versus 1.3 g/cm³ experimentally, and embedded iron increased from 63% to 71% during 1 ns of NPT simulation.
watch_item: The branched RF units were not cross-linked to one another, so the model does not yet establish the behavior of a fully connected aerogel network.
paper_title: An All-Atom Model of the Resorcinol-Formaldehyde Aerogel Skeleton from DFT and Molecular Dynamics: Validation and Iron Incorporation
